message_item_forms._note: `message` items come in exactly two shapes and the difference is turn-scope, not role.

base_form.meaning: The turn-independent system prompt. No `id`, no internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough. Byte-identical across the prewarm frame and the turn frame of a session, and identical across the gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-5.6-luna sessions (same sha256, 17730 chars) — it is the cacheable prefix.

turn_scoped_form.meaning: Everything produced by or for a specific turn: the per-turn developer context blocks (<app-context>, the /root multi-agent brief, <multi_agent_mode>), the <recommended_plugins> block, and the user`s own message. `id` is `msg_<uuid v7>` and the passthrough is {"turn_id": "<uuid v7>"} — all items of one turn share that turn_id.

observations: The developer system prompt begins `You are Codex, an agent based on GPT-5.` — the model family in that sentence is `GPT-5`, not the wire model name `gpt-5.6-sol`.
A turn opener carries 6 content parts on its first turn-scoped developer item (5027/16556/4757/966/646/1014 chars); the count is user-state dependent and is not a fingerprint.
Because the base form has no id, a proxy that regenerates ids per item must leave this one alone or it stops matching the cached prefix.
